selected_script.hook: Close-up of laundry covered in pet hair and lint after washing

script_record.pain_point: Pet hair and lint sticking to freshly washed laundry
script_record.conflict_hook: Frustrated user pulling hair-covered black shirt out of washer
script_record.product_solution: Absurd adult family rescuer places single floating hair filter directly into top-load wash water

timeline.scene: Close-up of a black cotton shirt covered in pet hair and lint in an open washing machine. No product.

timeline.purpose: 荒诞成年亲属携产品入场
timeline.scene: Grandmother in a full referee outfit enters frame holding one fully assembled floating filter with blue float domes and says 'Not on my watch!'
Filter is placed onto the water surface inside top-loader, floating steadily while long tapered white mesh bag catches floating lint.
Fast-cut showing clean floating action with water ripples and lint gathering safely inside the mesh bag.
Fast-cut in a different light laundry load showing clean clothes floating underneath without pet hair sticking.
Fast-cut showing the clean washed shirt being pulled out completely lint-free.
End frame text display: A simple upgrade for everyday use. Check it out today.

script_record.cta: A simple upgrade for everyday use. Check it out today.

final_moyin_jobs.promptText:
Create a 10-second vertical UGC ad video.
Timeline:
0-1.5s: Show one real daily pain point through a close-up detail: wet black laundry covered in stubborn pet hair inside an open top-loading washing machine. No product and no rescuer.
1.5-3s: An absurd adult grandmother wearing a sports referee jersey enters carrying the exact product—one fully assembled floating filter unit with a white circular outer ring, exactly four attached sky-blue hemispherical float domes (one center, three outer at 120 degrees), and one long tapered white mesh bag—from the first frame, places it directly on the water surface, and says 'Not on my watch!'
3-6s: Quickly show the product as the direct solution floating steadily on the water surface near gentle ripples, mesh bag submerged catching loose floating debris.
6-10s: Fast-cut scene 1 showing the first clear result of debris floating into the mesh cone while clothes move below.
Do not start with a perfect product shot.
Do not end with a CTA in this segment.
Keep the pacing fast, clear, low-risk, and product-focused.
Use the provided product reference images as the exact product identity.
Do not change the product color, shape, material, size ratio, logo position, texture, or visible structure.
Do not invent extra accessories, buttons, lights, packaging, or exaggerated functions.
Use the detail and side reference image to preserve product material, side structure, edge shape, texture, and visible details.
Use the function reference image only to understand the real product usage. Do not invent new functions.
